intro: A population pyramid is a country’s story on its side: the base is this year’s babies, the top is its oldest people. Drag the mother to set how many children women have, set how long people live, and watch the base of the pyramid, and then the rows above it, change: the base is the future population.
howItWorks:
The pyramid in Explore is computed, not drawn by hand: the population that the children per woman and the life expectancy you set lead to once they have held for a long time, with no migration (a stable population). Survival to each age comes from a model life table with exactly that life expectancy, so replacement level rises above 2.1 where many children die. Each row is the percent of all people in that 5 year band (men left, women right), at one scale for every setting. A teaching model, not any one country.

Growth rate = (crude birth rate − crude death rate) / 10, as a percent, and the doubling time is 70 divided by it: the same recipes as the course questions (ApEnvCalc). In Test yourself the pyramids are a model fitted to rounded United Nations shares (under 15 and 65 and over), and the drill numbers are invented for practice and recomputed by a checker on 300 problems per scenario.
